hints: Notice the counterweight is given as a $5000\text{ kg}$ mass while the load is given as a $12.0\text{ kN}$ force at $17.0\text{ m}$ from the pivot.
For equilibrium the clockwise moment from the $12.0\text{ kN}$ load must equal the anticlockwise moment from the counterweight weight about the pivot.
First convert the $5000\text{ kg}$ mass to weight in $\text{N}$ with $W = mg$, convert $12.0\text{ kN}$ to $\text{N}$, then use $F \times d$ on both sides.
walkthrough: Identify the pivot and the two moments: the $12.0\text{ kN}$ load at $17.0\text{ m}$ to the right tends to rotate one way, the counterweight at distance $d$ to the left tends to rotate the opposite way.
State the equilibrium condition: sum of clockwise moments equals sum of anticlockwise moments, so $W_{counter} \times d = W_{load} \times 17.0\text{ m}$.
Convert to consistent force units. Load force is $12.0\text{ kN} = 12000\text{ N}$. Counterweight weight is $W_{counter} = mg = 5000 \times 9.81 \approx 49050\text{ N}$.
Substitute into the moment equation: $49050 \times d = 12000 \times 17.0 = 204000\text{ N m}$.
Solve for $d$: $d = 204000 / 49050 \approx 4.16\text{ m}$, with units of $\text{m}$ as expected for a distance. This is option C.

options.A: Gives $0.0408\text{ m}$ by using $12.0\text{ N}$ instead of $12000\text{ N}$ for the load, mixing $\text{N}$ with $\text{kN}$.
options.B: Gives $0.240\text{ m}$ by inverting the moment balance, effectively calculating counterweight moment divided by load moment.
options.C: Balances moments about the pivot with $W \times d = 12000 \times 17.0$, giving $d \approx 4.16\text{ m}$.
options.D: Gives $40.8\text{ m}$ by using $5000\text{ N}$ for the counterweight, forgetting to multiply the $5000\text{ kg}$ mass by $g$.
